author: South Middlesex Times
title: Rep. Frank Pallone criticizes Trump's AI orders and meets new Rutgers president
text:
Frank Pallone U.S. House of Representatives from New Jersey | Official U.S. House Headshot
Frank Pallone U.S. House of Representatives from New Jersey | Official U.S. House Headshot
Rep. Frank Pallone, who represents New Jersey’s 6th district in the U.S. Congress, posted a series of updates on July 23, 2025, addressing issues ranging from artificial intelligence policy to higher education leadership.
In one post, Pallone criticized recent executive orders by former President Donald Trump regarding artificial intelligence. On July 23, he wrote: "Trump's AI executive orders prioritize corporate profits over people. It once again adopts Silicon Valley's failed 'move fast and break things' model that threatens people’s privacy and security while raising energy costs for everyday people. We can harness the promise of AI".
Earlier that day, Pallone shared a link to his full release without further comment: "Read my full release: https://t.co/plahfU6Nqq" (July 23).
Later in the evening, Pallone highlighted his meeting with Rutgers University’s new president and expressed optimism about future collaboration. He stated on July 23: "Great to meet @RutgersU new President William Tate in DC today. Looking forward to working with him to ensure Rutgers and New Jersey continue to lead the nation in academics, research, and development. Was also nice running into fellow Rutgers alum @DarrenSoto!"
Pallone has represented New Jersey’s 6th District since 1988 after succeeding James J. Howard and previously served in the New Jersey Senate from 1984 to 1988. Born in Long Branch in 1951, he continues to reside there at age 71. His educational background includes a BA from Middlebury College (1973) and a JD from Rutgers University-Camden (1978).
